title: Subject–Verb Agreement
orientation: Agreement becomes difficult when a long subject contains several nouns, when a group can be understood as one body or as individuals, or when a subject appears after its verb. This lesson starts with the ordinary person-and-number patterns, then develops these more demanding cases. You will learn why the quality of the answers is singular while a number of answers are plural, and why legitimate British collective agreement cannot be replaced by a universal singular rule. You will also inspect each clause separately, especially when a relative pronoun refers to a noun inside a longer subject. In the practice, state the subject, its intended interpretation and the relevant convention before changing a verb. When two readings remain defensible, explain the ambiguity or rewrite the sentence clearly rather than inventing an error.
outcomes: Identify the finite verb and its agreement controller in long subjects.
Distinguish coordination, accompaniment and notional agreement.
Explain collective and indefinite-pronoun patterns with regional and register qualifications.
Analyse relative-clause, inverted and existential agreement.
Choose agreement for quantities, measures, titles and plural-looking nouns without absolute shortcuts.

modules.title: Person, number and the structure of the subject
modules.definition: Subject–verb agreement is the correspondence between a subject’s grammatical person and number and the finite verb forms that show those distinctions. Agreement depends on structure and interpretation, not simply the nearest visible noun.
foundation: Compare The guard checks the door and The guards check the door. In present simple, an ordinary lexical verb normally adds -s with a third-person singular subject. I and you use the base form even when referring to one person: I check; you check. Be has am, is and are in the present and was and were in the past. Have has has with a third-person singular subject. Most other past-tense verbs do not change for number: the guard checked and the guards checked. Agreement therefore does not mean adding an ending to every verb in every sentence.
intermediate: Find the complete subject and its head, the central noun in an ordinary noun phrase. In The condition of the external walls is worrying, condition is the head; walls occurs inside a modifying of-phrase. A relative clause or parenthetical phrase also does not normally replace that head as agreement controller: The folder that contains the photographs is missing. When auxiliaries occur, the finite auxiliary carries the relevant agreement: The folders have been moved. Do not alter moved to make it plural. Subject identification is a structural analysis; merely crossing out every prepositional phrase can remove information needed to interpret the sentence.
advanced: Coordination with and normally creates a plural subject: The clerk and the porter are waiting. An accompanying phrase such as together with, as well as or along with is not ordinary subject coordination: The clerk, together with two porters, is waiting. If two descriptions identify a single individual, the subject may be interpreted as singular: The founder and treasurer is one person in this organisation. If the founder and the treasurer are different people, use plural agreement. Articles and context help identify the intended reference; do not decide identity from a memorised surface formula alone.
expert: The familiar head-noun rule is a reliable starting point for ordinary noun phrases, not an exhaustive theory of English agreement. Quantificational constructions, collectives and notional readings require further analysis in later modules. Distinguish genuine coordination from a phrase merely mentioning another person. Also distinguish the subject from an object or predicative complement: The main difficulty is the missing records does not make records the subject of is in this ordinary clause. Where the number or identity of coordinated referents is unclear, rewriting to make that identity explicit is often better than defending an ambiguous choice by rule recital.

patterns.form: third-person singular subject + present verb in -s
patterns.meaning: A common present-simple agreement pattern; be and some verbs have special forms.

patterns.form: head noun + modifying phrase + finite verb
patterns.meaning: In an ordinary noun phrase, the modifier does not replace the head as agreement controller.

examples.sentence: The colour of the curtains has faded.
examples.analysis: Singular colour controls has; curtains is inside the of-phrase.

examples.sentence: The inspectors have been reviewing the photographs.
examples.analysis: Plural inspectors controls finite have; the other forms do not acquire plural endings.

examples.sentence: The director, as well as two advisers, is attending.
examples.analysis: As well as introduces an accompanying phrase rather than a second coordinated subject.

contrasts.a: The designer and the builder are different people.
contrasts.b: The designer and builder is available; in this project both roles are performed by the same person.
contrasts.note: Both can be grammatical with the explicitly different reference. Agreement follows the intended subject organisation and identity.

exceptions: Most lexical past-tense forms do not distinguish singular and plural: The driver arrived and The drivers arrived. Do not manufacture a plural past ending.

mistakes.problem: The schedule of public hearings are available.
mistakes.repair: The schedule of public hearings is available.
mistakes.reason: Singular schedule is the ordinary subject head.

mistakes.problem: The manager, along with two assistants, have signed the letter.
mistakes.repair: The manager, along with two assistants, has signed the letter.
mistakes.reason: The accompanying phrase does not ordinarily make the singular subject plural.

glossary.definition: The subject expression whose person and number determine a relevant finite verb form.
glossary.example: The form of have in The files have arrived is controlled by files.

glossary.definition: Reference other than to the speaker as I/we or the addressee as you.
glossary.example: She and the committee are third-person expressions.

modules.title: Collectives, indefinite pronouns and competing agreement cues
modules.definition: English agreement can reflect grammatical form, the meaning of a group, or proximity in particular coordinated patterns. Collective nouns and quantifying pronouns require qualified guidance about reference, register and established regional variation.
foundation: A collective noun names a group: team, government, committee, family. In British English, singular agreement commonly presents the group as a unit, while plural agreement can present its members: The committee has issued its report; The committee have changed their minds. American English more often uses singular agreement with these ordinary group nouns, especially when acting as one unit. This is a broad convention rather than a claim that every collective has identical behaviour in all varieties. Police ordinarily takes plural agreement: The police are investigating. Do not transfer a rule for committee blindly to police.
intermediate: Indefinite pronouns and determiners form different patterns. Everyone, somebody, nobody and each ordinarily take singular finite agreement: Everyone is ready; Each of the rooms has a window. Both, few, many and several are plural in their ordinary countable uses. Singular they can refer back to a grammatically singular person expression without changing its verb: Everyone has their own ticket. All, some and most depend on what is quantified: Some of the water is contaminated; Some of the wells are contaminated. None can also support singular or plural interpretation, particularly when referring to a countable set.
advanced: Neither of and either of commonly take singular agreement in careful formal prose: Neither of the plans is suitable. Plural agreement occurs in established conversational usage, especially when a plural noun phrase is close to the verb; a register-sensitive exercise should identify its target convention. With subjects joined by or or nor, a common editing convention makes the verb agree with the nearer coordinated part: Neither the director nor the assistants are available; Neither the assistants nor the director is available. Recast awkward combinations, particularly those mixing person, rather than assuming proximity alone makes every possible sequence elegant or uncontroversial.
expert: Notional agreement follows an interpretation of number rather than surface form alone. Proximity agreement follows a nearby eligible expression in constructions where that convention is established. These should not be confused with accidental agreement attraction, as in The cost of the repairs are high in ordinary formal prose. Collective pronouns should make the intended unit-versus-members reference clear across the passage, though a writer may deliberately shift perspective when context supports it. None of is especially unsuitable for an absolute always-singular rule: authoritative usage accounts describe both singular and plural verbs. State the desired register and interpretation when a task depends on the choice.

patterns.meaning: Possible unit/member contrast, particularly in British English; conventions vary by noun and variety.

patterns.form: each/everyone + singular verb; both/several + plural verb
patterns.meaning: Ordinary agreement of these specific quantifying expressions.

examples.analysis: Everyone takes singular has; singular their provides inclusive personal reference.

examples.sentence: The committee have not agreed among themselves.
examples.analysis: British plural agreement foregrounds the members’ differing views.

examples.sentence: Neither the secretary nor the assistants are free.
examples.analysis: Plural are follows the common nearer-subject convention, with assistants nearest.

contrasts.a: The team is improving its public image.
contrasts.b: The team are arguing among themselves.
contrasts.note: Both are established in British English. The first treats the team as a unit; the second foregrounds members.

exceptions: None of the candidates is available and None of the candidates are available both occur in standard usage; guidance differs in its preferred register. A trustworthy answer key must not reject one without an explicitly justified criterion.

mistakes.problem: Each of the windows have a safety lock.
mistakes.repair: Each of the windows has a safety lock.
mistakes.reason: Each is the singular quantifying subject.

mistakes.problem: The police is questioning the witnesses, in ordinary standard usage.
mistakes.repair: The police are questioning the witnesses.
mistakes.reason: Police ordinarily has plural agreement, unlike many singular-form collective nouns.

glossary.definition: Agreement influenced by the interpreted number or organisation of the referent.
glossary.example: Three years is a long time treats the period as one measure.

glossary.definition: An unintended agreement choice influenced by a nearby noun that is not the ordinary controller.
glossary.example: In The quality of the copies are poor, plural copies attracts are away from singular quality.

modules.title: Relative clauses, inversion and existential constructions
modules.definition: Each clause has its own agreement relationships. Relative-clause verbs follow the intended antecedent, and inversion can place a subject after an auxiliary or verb. Existential there introduces an additional construction whose formal agreement commonly follows its postverbal noun phrase.
foundation: In The drivers who work nights receive an allowance, the relative pronoun who refers to plural drivers, so its clause uses work. The main clause also has plural drivers as its subject. In The driver who works nights receives an allowance, both relevant subjects are singular. Analyse the clauses separately; the verb of one clause does not mechanically control the other. A longer subject can contain a plural antecedent inside a singular outer phrase: One of the drivers who work nights receives an allowance. Outer one controls receives, while drivers supplies the usual antecedent for who work nights.
intermediate: Expressions such as one of those people who usually select a relative clause describing the plural group: She is one of those people who notice everything. A relative attached specifically to the individual one has a different interpretation and may take a singular verb. The only one of the drivers who has a permit normally singles out the one permitted individual. Do not decide all relative attachments from the presence of the word only alone. Where the intended scope is important, make it explicit: She is the only driver who has a permit; among the permitted drivers, she is the only one available.
advanced: In questions, the subject often follows a finite auxiliary: Are the documents ready? Does the document contain a signature? In locative inversion, the subject can follow the lexical verb: On the shelf were three sealed boxes. Find boxes before selecting were. Existential There is a problem and There are several problems conventionally match the form of be to the postverbal noun phrase in careful formal writing. Contracted There’s several problems is widespread in conversation; revise it to There are several problems for the stated formal convention without presenting all conversational occurrences as evidence of ignorance.
expert: Grammatical frameworks differ in analysing existential there: many modern accounts treat it as a dummy subject, while traditional teaching calls the following noun phrase the real subject. Both descriptions can support the same practical formal-agreement guidance if terminology is made explicit. Not every word after a verb is a subject: compare On the desk lies the report with The clerk filed the report. Negative inversion also leaves agreement with the actual subject: Never have the records been so clear. Parsing requires clause structure and reference, not an instruction to choose whichever noun is closest to the finite verb.

patterns.meaning: Relative-clause agreement reflects the intended antecedent.

patterns.form: There is + singular noun phrase; There are + plural noun phrase
patterns.meaning: Common careful formal pattern in existential be-constructions.

examples.sentence: One of the books that explain the method is missing.
examples.analysis: Books controls explain in the relative; one controls main-clause is.

examples.sentence: Near the entrance stand two noticeboards.
examples.analysis: Plural noticeboards follows stand and is its subject.

examples.sentence: There are three reasons why the proposal needs revision.
examples.analysis: The plural postverbal noun phrase selects are in this formal existential construction.

contrasts.a: The only driver who has a permit is waiting.
contrasts.b: One of the drivers who have permits is waiting.
contrasts.note: Both are grammatical with different relative-clause antecedents: driver versus drivers. The main waiting subject is singular in each.

exceptions: Informal contracted there’s commonly introduces plural associates. For formal prose, use the agreed full form; distinguish register-sensitive editing from a universal ban on attested conversational grammar.

mistakes.problem: One of the students who lives on this corridor are absent; intended meaning: several students live on the corridor, one is absent.
mistakes.repair: One of the students who live on this corridor is absent.
mistakes.reason: The stated context makes students the relative antecedent and one the main agreement controller.

mistakes.problem: Beside the printer was two unopened boxes.
mistakes.repair: Beside the printer were two unopened boxes.
mistakes.reason: Plural boxes is the postverbal subject in the locative inversion.

glossary.definition: The expression to which a referring item, such as a relative pronoun, is related.
glossary.example: Drivers is the antecedent of who in drivers who work nights.

glossary.definition: A construction introducing the existence or presence of a situation or entity, often with dummy there.
glossary.example: There are two exits introduces the exits.

modules.title: Quantities, measures, titles and plural-looking forms
modules.definition: Agreement with a quantity depends on what is measured or counted and how it is construed. The spelling of a noun, a percentage or a numerical expression does not by itself establish the number required in every use.
foundation: Some nouns look plural but take singular agreement in their ordinary meanings: The news is encouraging; Mathematics is compulsory. Other nouns normally take plural agreement: The trousers are wet; The scissors are blunt. A pair of scissors is different because pair is singular: This pair of scissors is blunt. Series has the same spelling in singular and plural: This series is useful; These two series are useful. Use determiners, meaning and a learner’s dictionary where the form alone is misleading. Do not add an invented singular police or a plural news merely to make the ending match a simplified pattern.
intermediate: Fractions and percentages commonly follow the number interpretation of the of-complement: Half of the water is gone; Half of the bottles are empty; Twenty per cent of the applicants were absent. A percentage without an explicit complement still requires context: Twenty per cent is a substantial share treats the proportion as one amount. If the complement is a collective, its own possible unit/member readings can matter. A number of applications have arrived is a conventional plural quantifying construction; The number of applications has risen treats number as the quantity being discussed. These are different structures, not contradictory examples of the same rule.
advanced: A measure phrase can denote one amount: Ten kilometres is too far to walk today; Three years is a long wait. Plural agreement remains natural when separate units or their passage are in view: Three years have passed. A title naming one work commonly receives singular agreement despite plural words inside it: Great Expectations is a novel. This does not make every plural proper name singular in every variety; team and organisation names may follow collective conventions. Mathematical statements also have conventional forms, such as Two plus two is four, but do not infer a universal rule for every coordinated numerical expression.
expert: Meaning can change the number behaviour of the same spelling. Statistics is difficult can name a discipline; The statistics are misleading refers to numerical figures. Politics can name an academic topic or a person’s views, with differing agreement: Her politics are well known. Such contrasts illustrate why grammatical number, semantic quantity and lexical convention must be distinguished. A rigid instruction to make the verb agree with the nearest noun fails with The number of files is increasing; an unrestricted head-noun slogan also needs qualification for quantifying A number of files are missing. Analyse the construction, then state which meaning and editorial convention support the chosen verb.

patterns.meaning: Agreement commonly follows the relevant mass or count interpretation.

patterns.form: a number of + plural noun + plural verb; the number of + plural noun + singular verb
patterns.meaning: Conventional contrast between quantifying several items and discussing their number.

examples.sentence: Half of the evidence is missing.
examples.analysis: Evidence is a mass noun here, so the fraction has singular agreement.

examples.sentence: Half of the witnesses are waiting outside.
examples.analysis: The fraction ranges over plural people, giving plural agreement.

examples.sentence: The number of reports has doubled, although a number of reports are still incomplete.
examples.analysis: The first subject concerns a figure; the second quantifies several reports.

contrasts.a: Statistics is part of the syllabus.
contrasts.b: The statistics are based on last year’s survey.
contrasts.note: Both are grammatical: the discipline differs from a set of figures.

exceptions: A period can be construed as one measure or as separate years whose passage is asserted: Three years is a long time and Three years have passed are both ordinary. Do not impose singular agreement on every expression containing a measurement.

mistakes.problem: The news are more encouraging this week.
mistakes.repair: The news is more encouraging this week.
mistakes.reason: News ordinarily takes singular agreement despite its ending.

mistakes.problem: This series of seminars are intended for new staff.
mistakes.repair: This series of seminars is intended for new staff.
mistakes.reason: This identifies a singular series; seminars is inside its modifier.

glossary.definition: A grammatical singular/plural distinction that is not always predictable from real-world quantity or spelling.
glossary.example: News has singular agreement despite final -s.

glossary.definition: A construction whose purpose is to express an amount or number of referents.
glossary.example: A number of complaints means several complaints.

questions.prompt: The condition of the outer walls ____ deteriorating. Use the ordinary singular head-noun agreement.
questions.why: Singular condition is the subject head; walls belongs to its modifying of-phrase.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes most ordinary lexical past-tense forms?
options: They add -s for every plural subject.
They do not normally distinguish singular from plural: she arrived / they arrived.
They require a plural participle after every plural noun.
They are all identical to present-tense forms.
questions.why: Most lexical past forms show no number contrast; be is an important exception.

questions.prompt: For ordinary British English usage, which analysis is accurate?
options: A committee can take singular unit agreement or plural member agreement.
Plural collective agreement proves that the noun is grammatically misspelled.
Collective nouns must always take singular verbs.
Police always takes the same agreement as committee.
questions.why: British English permits unit/member agreement with many collective nouns; the behaviour of individual nouns and varieties needs qualification.

questions.prompt: Review the intended inclusive statement: Everyone has their own copy. Which judgement is accurate?
options: Their is impossible after a singular antecedent in all standard English.
No error: everyone takes has, while singular their supplies inclusive reference.
Change has to have because their is plural in spelling.
questions.why: The singular finite agreement belongs to everyone. Established singular they/their can supply inclusive personal reference.

questions.prompt: Choose careful formal existential agreement: There ____ several practical difficulties.
questions.why: The plural postverbal noun phrase takes are in the target formal pattern. Informal there’s with a plural is a separate register-sensitive use.

questions.prompt: One of the books that ____ the method is missing. The relative clause explicitly describes the plural group of books.
questions.why: The stated antecedent of that is plural books, so explain is appropriate. Outer one separately takes main-clause is.

questions.prompt: Half of the evidence ____ missing.
questions.why: Evidence is a mass noun in this use, so the fraction takes singular is.

questions.prompt: The number of completed applications ____ risen.
questions.why: The number names a single figure, so has is the ordinary agreement choice. A number of applications have … is a different quantifying construction.

questions.prompt: Which pair correctly contrasts the discipline with numerical figures?
options: Statistics be demanding; these statistics am incomplete.
Statistics have demanding; these statistics has incomplete.
Statistics is demanding; these statistics are incomplete.
Statistics are demanding as a discipline; these statistics is incomplete.
questions.why: The academic discipline takes singular agreement; the demonstratively identified figures are plural.

questions.prompt: Which statement about None of the candidates is/are available is most reliable?
options: Only are has ever been standard.
Both singular and plural agreement occur; interpretation and register guidance should be stated.
questions.why: Authorities record both singular and plural agreement with none of a countable set. A context-free absolute prohibition is unreliable.

questions.prompt: In The quality of the printed maps has improved, identify the subject head and explain has.
questions.model: Quality is the singular head of the subject noun phrase; of the printed maps modifies it, so has has singular agreement.
rubric: Identify quality rather than maps.
Connect the head to the finite auxiliary has.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

questions.prompt: Complete: I ____ ready; the secretary ____ ready; the secretaries ____ ready. Use present forms of be.
questions.model: I am ready; the secretary is ready; the secretaries are ready.
rubric: Use am with I, is with the singular secretary and are with plural secretaries.
Recognise that one person referred to by I does not select is.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

questions.prompt: Explain the agreement difference between The captain and the medic are waiting and The captain, along with the medic, is waiting.
questions.model: And coordinates two subject referents, giving plural agreement. Along with adds an accompanying phrase to the singular subject captain, giving ordinary singular agreement.
rubric: Distinguish coordination from accompaniment.
Identify the relevant controller in each sentence.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

questions.prompt: The founder and treasurer is attending. What information would help decide whether the singular is appropriate?
questions.model: Determine whether founder and treasurer describe the same person or two different people. A single individual can support singular agreement; separate coordinated people normally take plural agreement.
rubric: Ask about referential identity.
Avoid deciding identity solely from the absence of a second article.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

questions.prompt: Explain the unit/member contrast in The committee has published its report and The committee are discussing their individual objections.
questions.model: The first presents a single institutional action and unit reference; the second is established British usage foregrounding the members and their individual objections.
rubric: Recognise legitimate British plural collective agreement.
Explain the interpretation behind the pronouns as well as the verb.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

questions.prompt: Use the usual careful formal convention: Each of the folders ____ a label. Choose a form of have.
questions.model: Each of the folders has a label.
rubric: Use singular has with each.
Do not let plural folders inside the of-phrase control the verb.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

questions.prompt: Explain why Some of the medicine is missing and Some of the tablets are missing take different verbs.
questions.model: Medicine is mass in this context; tablets is plural countable. The quantified expression reflects the relevant number interpretation.
rubric: Identify the mass/count distinction.
Avoid claiming that some always takes the same number.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

questions.prompt: Apply the ordinary nearer-subject editing convention, then offer a smoother rewrite: Neither the assistants nor the director ____ available.
questions.model: Neither the assistants nor the director is available. A clearer alternative is The assistants are unavailable, and so is the director.
rubric: Use singular is with nearer director under the stated convention.
Offer a rewrite preserving that neither party is available.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

questions.prompt: Analyse both agreement relationships in One of the residents who work nights has complained. The intended relative describes several residents.
questions.model: Residents is the antecedent of who, so work is plural. One is the singular outer subject, so the main clause uses has.
rubric: Identify two clauses and controllers.
Use the stated antecedent rather than automatically agreeing every verb with one.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

questions.prompt: Reconstruct the formal inverted sentence: near the doorway / two guards / were / standing.
questions.model: Near the doorway were standing two guards.
rubric: Place plural two guards as the postverbal subject in the requested inversion.
Keep were agreeing with guards.
alternatives: Near the doorway, two guards were standing is grammatical normal order; if used, explain that it does not retain the requested inversion.

questions.prompt: Explain why There’s two seats left may occur in conversation but There are two seats left is the normal formal edit.
questions.model: Contracted there’s commonly introduces plural associates in speech. Careful formal agreement normally uses are with plural two seats.
rubric: Distinguish conversational attestation from the target formal convention.
Avoid calling the conversational speaker unintelligent or the pattern impossible.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

questions.prompt: Compare The only resident who works nights has complained and One of the residents who work nights has complained.
questions.model: The first relative identifies a singular resident; the second relative describes a plural group. Each complete main subject is singular, so both main clauses use has.
rubric: Identify resident versus residents as the relevant antecedents.
Keep relative-clause agreement separate from main-clause agreement.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

questions.prompt: Complete: Half of the water ____ gone; half of the bottles ____ empty; this pair of scissors ____ blunt.
questions.model: Half of the water is gone; half of the bottles are empty; this pair of scissors is blunt.
rubric: Use singular with mass water and singular pair.
Use plural with the counted bottles.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

questions.prompt: Explain the different subjects in A number of appeals are pending and The number of appeals is increasing.
questions.model: A number of appeals quantifies several appeals and takes plural agreement. The number of appeals makes the numerical figure the subject and takes singular agreement.
rubric: Distinguish quantifying several items from discussing a figure.
Do not use the word closest to the verb as the sole test.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

questions.prompt: Use context to classify series: This series is complete. These two series are incomplete.
questions.model: Series has an unchanged singular/plural spelling. This identifies one series; these two identifies two series. The verbs reflect those different numbers.
rubric: Use determiner and quantity clues.
Do not assume final -s proves plural number.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

questions.prompt: Explain why Three years is a long wait and Three years have passed can both be grammatical.
questions.model: The first treats the period as one measure; the second presents the passage of plural years. Agreement depends on the construction and interpretation, not an unconditional measurement rule.
rubric: Recognise both established constructions.
Explain the difference in construal.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

questions.prompt: Edit only real agreement faults: The news are encouraging. The police are checking the entrances. A number of reports has arrived.
questions.model: The news is encouraging. The police are checking the entrances. A number of reports have arrived.
rubric: Use singular agreement with news.
Retain plural police are.
Use the plural quantifying a number of construction.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

questions.prompt: Write one sentence with everyone and inclusive their, and one with both. Explain the finite agreement in each.
questions.model: Everyone has their own timetable. Everyone controls singular has. Both are available after lunch. Both controls plural are.
rubric: Use singular finite agreement with everyone despite singular their.
Use plural agreement with both.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

corrections.prompt: Correct: The cost of the replacement windows have increased.
corrections.model: The cost of the replacement windows has increased.
rubric: Identify singular cost as controller.
Retain the plural windows inside the modifier.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

corrections.prompt: Correct under ordinary formal agreement: Each of the candidates have a reference number.
corrections.model: Each of the candidates has a reference number.
rubric: Use singular has with each.
Do not change the intended several candidates into a single candidate.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

corrections.prompt: Correct: The police is searching the warehouse.
corrections.model: The police are searching the warehouse.
rubric: Use the ordinary plural agreement of police.
Keep the progressive search construction.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

corrections.prompt: Correct the two faults for the stated meaning: One of the workers who repairs these lifts have arrived. Several workers repair them; one has arrived.
corrections.model: One of the workers who repair these lifts has arrived.
rubric: Use plural repair with the stated plural worker group.
Use singular has with outer one.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

corrections.prompt: Correct for careful formal writing: There is several unsigned forms on the desk.
corrections.model: There are several unsigned forms on the desk.
rubric: Use formal are with plural forms.
Keep the existential construction and stated location.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

corrections.prompt: Correct: The number of missing files are alarming.
corrections.model: The number of missing files is alarming.
rubric: Make the figure expressed by the number the agreement controller.
Do not change the claim into several files being alarming.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

corrections.prompt: Decide whether a change is required in British English: The committee have changed their minds after discussing the evidence.
corrections.model: No change is required. The plural collective agreement and their minds foreground the members in an established British pattern.
rubric: Recognise a legitimate member reading.
Do not replace their minds with its mind and alter the intended reference.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

corrections.prompt: Decide whether a change is required: These two series of workshops are fully booked.
corrections.model: No change is required. Two series is plural despite the unchanged spelling, so are is appropriate.
rubric: Use the stated quantity two.
Do not make every occurrence of series singular.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

transformations.prompt: Split into two sentences without changing the facts: The manager, who is accompanied by two consultants at today’s meeting, has approved the plan. Keep the manager as the singular subject of the approval clause.
transformations.model: The manager has approved the plan. Two consultants are accompanying the manager at today’s meeting.
rubric: Retain the manager as the stated approval subject.
Preserve the consultants’ accompanying presence at today’s meeting without adding that they approved.
alternatives: The manager has approved the plan. At today’s meeting, the manager is accompanied by two consultants.

transformations.prompt: Avoid the awkward mixed-number nor-subject while preserving both negative facts: Neither the director nor the assistants are available.
transformations.model: The director is unavailable, and the assistants are unavailable.
rubric: Keep both parties unavailable.
Give each clause agreement with its own explicit subject.
alternatives: The director is not available, and neither are the assistants.

writing.prompt: Write a 90–130-word briefing about an inspection. Include a singular subject with a plural of-phrase, a plural coordinated subject, a quantified mass noun, a plural counted group, and a collective noun whose unit/member interpretation is clear. Explain any regional convention you choose.
writing.model:
The condition of the external walls is the main concern. The engineer and the site manager are preparing a repair plan. Half of the evidence is already available, but several photographs are still missing. A number of residents have requested a meeting, and the number of requests has increased since Monday. The committee has issued its preliminary report as a single body. Its members are now considering their individual objections. There are two possible dates for the next inspection. The final timetable will identify who is responsible for each task and how the outstanding evidence will be collected.

Analysis: Condition controls is; engineer and site manager controls are; evidence is mass, while photographs and residents are plural count nouns. The committee is presented as one body, followed by explicit reference to its members; this unit/member distinction is compatible with the British editorial convention.
rubric: Identify each subject and the finite verb it controls.
Distinguish a number of from the number of.
Match the mass/count quantity interpretation.
Keep collective unit/member reference clear and accept an established regional convention.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

recall.prompt: Recall Day 2: Why is equipment not automatically plural when it refers to several machines?
recall.model: Equipment is ordinarily a mass noun in this sense; several items of equipment counts units without treating equipment itself as a regular plural.
rubric: Distinguish semantic quantity from grammatical countability.
Use a suitable unit expression.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

recall.prompt: Recall Day 4: Does singular they require everyone to take have in Everyone has their ticket?
recall.model: No. Everyone controls singular has; singular their supplies personal reference without changing the antecedent’s finite agreement.
rubric: Keep pronoun reference and finite agreement distinct.
Recognise established singular they/their.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

recall.prompt: Recall Day 5: In The reports have been filed, which word is finite and can show the relevant singular/plural distinction?
recall.model: Have is finite; the corresponding singular subject would use has. Been and filed are participial forms here.
rubric: Identify have as finite.
Explain the has/have contrast without changing participles.
alternatives: Accept other grammatical responses that preserve the stated facts, viewpoint and relevant distinction.

checklist: I identify the subject of each clause before correcting its verb.
I distinguish number, countability and real-world quantity.
I explain collective and none/neither variation rather than automatically rejecting unfamiliar forms.
I preserve meaning when restructuring an awkward coordinated subject.
I review original writing separately from objective recognition.
